key_insight: A frozen, general-purpose LLM can propose promising low-energy quantum circuit parameters for structured Hamiltonians, but performs worse than Adam optimization on general random Hamiltonians.
engineering_relevance: LLM-generated circuit parameters enable independently verifiable energy calculations, offering a more physically grounded approach than direct LLM energy predictions.
method: Generate complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions.
Test optional iterative energy feedback across random, structured parent, and molecular Hamiltonians.
Probe blind circuit interpretation through algorithm identification and measurement-outcome prediction.
evidence_signal: Evaluations found larger energy errors than Adam on general Hamiltonians, limited gains from feedback, and promising low-energy configurations for structured Hamiltonians.
watch_item: Direct LLM minimum-energy predictions can violate spectral lower bounds; independently evaluate energies from generated circuit parameters.
paper_title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
